html:
Ciboney is a name used for early peoples of Cuba and nearby islands of the Greater Antilles before and alongside the Taíno. The map uses it for Cuba and Hispaniola in 800 and 900.

Who the Ciboney were is debated. Spanish writers such as Bartolomé de las Casas described a people in Cuba who served the Taíno chiefs. Later archaeologists used the name for the old fishing and gathering cultures of the islands, people without pottery or farming who had lived there for thousands of years. Today many scholars think the Ciboney of Spanish times were a western Taíno group who spoke a dialect of the Taíno language, and they prefer other names for the earlier peoples.

The far west of Cuba held another people, the Guanahatabey, who lived by fishing and gathering. All of these peoples were devastated by Spanish conquest, forced labour and disease in the early 1500s. See also Caribbean hunter-gatherers.
sum: Ciboney is a name used for early peoples of Cuba and nearby islands of the Greater Antilles before and alongside the Taíno. The map uses it for Cuba and Hispaniola in 800 and 900.
